summary: Tenant resharding triggered continuous-batcher tick skew causing intermittent p95/p99 latency cliffs
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled tenant resharding that redistributed weight across worker pools, NimbleAI reported intermittent p95/p99 latency cliffs and sporadic 504 timeouts for a subset of API keys. The pattern appeared as waves: normal latency for ~10-20 minutes, then 30-90s windows of elevated p95/p99 and occasional request timeouts. Impact: Customer observed degraded user experience on production traffic with automated throttling engaged; several live sessions timed out and some inference jobs retried, increasing cost. Environment: Dedicated tenancy for NimbleAI in prod us-east; dedicated GPU pool, continuous-batcher enabled with tenant-aware coalescing and KV cache warmup. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a tenant weight rebalance (resharding) on dedicated pool. 2) Send steady low-QPS short-sequence traffic (median token length ~25) from multiple API keys. 3) Observe continuous-batcher flush schedule and per-tenant tick alignment. Observed behavior and logs: - Metrics: baseline p95 ~120ms, p99 ~280ms. During incident p95 rose to ~650-950ms and p99 spiked to 2.4-3.1s; 504s observed at ~0.6% of requests in the window. - Logs: worker:batcher: tick skew detected: tenant reweight applied while flush-timers active; "flush_delay=37ms -> jittered 370ms" repeated. - Traces: many requests show an extra scheduling hop where microbatches are transferred between batcher queues, adding ~300-800ms per request. Investigation notes: Hypothesis A: Resharding/weight-change path causes continuous-batcher to reassign tenant ownership mid-window, which resets its flush timers and introduces clustered flushes (coalescer fanout + requeue). Hypothesis B: Reassignment triggers KV-cache thrashing while new owner warms the cache, increasing token generation time for affected sequences. Early evidence favors Hypothesis A (tick/timer skew visible in batcher debug logs) with KV-cache contributing as a secondary factor for longer tails. Temporary mitigation applied: - Rolled back active reshard to previous weights for the affected pool at 2026-03-10T18:22Z. - Recycled 4 worker instances in the pool to clear stale batcher state. - Applied a short-term guard: throttle reshard frequency (min interval 15m) and defer weight pushes if active flush windows detected. Next steps / proposed fixes: 1) Engineering to implement per-tenant tick stabilization: ensure ownership transfer does not reset in-flight flush timers; add handoff protocol to drain microbatches before weight change. (PR referenced above.) 2) Add monitoring alert for batcher tick variance and cross-tenant reassign rate. 3) Run chaos tests simulating frequent resharding to validate fixes. 4) Consider pre-warm KV cache on target owner when reassigning heavy tenants. Follow-ups: schedule postmortem and update runbook to include resharding safety checks and required telemetry.
